semantic_correction.stem: An average-risk adult for whom colorectal cancer screening is indicated asks whether colonoscopy is the only screening option. Which response by the nurse is accurate?

options.A: Colonoscopy is the standard screening method, and stool-based tests are used only after an abnormal colonoscopy.
options.B: Several screening options are recommended, including stool-based tests and direct-visualization tests such as colonoscopy.
options.C: A surgical biopsy is required before colorectal cancer screening can begin in an asymptomatic average-risk adult.
options.D: Stool-based tests are mainly diagnostic tests used after colorectal cancer has already been confirmed.

semantic_correction.rationale: The current USPSTF colorectal-cancer screening recommendation lists several recommended screening strategies for average-risk adults, including stool-based tests such as FIT and stool DNA-FIT and direct-visualization tests such as colonoscopy, flexible sigmoidoscopy, and CT colonography. Colonoscopy is therefore one recommended option rather than the only screening method. Abnormal stool-based tests require follow-up colonoscopy, but stool tests are themselves recommended screening tests used before a cancer diagnosis is established.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Explain that colorectal cancer screening can be performed with several evidence-based strategies, including stool-based and direct-visualization tests, rather than colonoscopy alone.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: removed repeated 'only' distractor cueing, shortened and balanced the correct answer, and preserved the USPSTF distinction between recommended stool-based screening and direct-visualization screening with colonoscopy as one option rather than the sole method.

audit_findings_append.finding: The revised item accurately teaches that colonoscopy is one of several recommended colorectal-cancer screening strategies.

option_audit.A: Incorrect. Stool-based tests are recommended screening strategies and are not restricted to use after colonoscopy.
option_audit.B: Correct. USPSTF recommends both stool-based and direct-visualization screening options.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Screening does not require a surgical biopsy before recommended noninvasive or visualization tests can be used.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. Stool-based tests are screening tests used before diagnosis; abnormal results require follow-up colonoscopy.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. B alone accurately describes the range of current USPSTF screening strategies.
cueing_check: All four options are colorectal-screening statements of comparable length and specificity; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies B.
